error: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module
meaning: The browser tried to load a lazy-loaded JavaScript chunk that no longer exists. After a new deploy, the file names change (they include a hash), but users with the old page open still ask for the old files.
causes: You redeployed while users had the app open; the old chunk files were removed.
The host serves index.html for missing .js files (SPA fallback), so the browser gets HTML instead of JS.
A CDN or service worker cached the old index.html.
Wrong base path, so chunks are requested from the wrong URL.

steps.text: Reload once automatically when a chunk fails (Vite fires vite:preloadError).
Do not cache index.html; cache hashed assets for a long time. Netlify example (netlify.toml):
steps.code:
[[headers]]
  for = "/index.html"
  [headers.values]
    Cache-Control = "no-cache"
[[headers]]
  for = "/assets/*"
  [headers.values]
    Cache-Control = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"

steps.text: If the app lives under a subpath, set base in vite.config.ts (e.g. base: '/app/').
If you added a service worker/PWA plugin, make it update on new versions (registerType: 'autoUpdate').

prompt: After each deploy some users get 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module'. Add a vite:preloadError listener that reloads the page once (guarded with sessionStorage), set no-cache headers for index.html and long immutable caching for /assets, and check vite.config base is correct.

faq.a: Usually not; it's old tabs asking for deleted files after a deploy.
A hard refresh (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R) fixes it there.
